newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand orders suspension of 42 finance firms.
newsitem.headline: Thailand orders suspension of 42 finance firms.

text.p: Thailand's central bank on Tuesday said it has suspended more than half of its finance companies after saying finance firms have borrowed almost 500 billion baht ($16.13 billion) from the central bank to ease their liquidity problems.

Bank of Thailand governor Chaiyawat Wibulswadi told a news conference the bank had suspended operations of 42 finance companies, in addition to 16 already suspended. The bank also guaranteed debt repayments and deposits of the troubled companies.
Thai cash-strapped finance companies have been struggling to cope with higher funding costs and deteriorating revenues as Thailand's economic fundamentals have deteriorated.
Creditors and depositors at these firms will be protected, Chaiyawat said.
Promissory note depositors will be able to exchange their deposits at weaker firms for notes issued by stronger finance companies, he addded.

The bank suspended the operations of 16 ailing firms earlier this year. The new suspension is part of a series of measures aimed at boosting the economy in order to get assistance from the International Monetary Fund and foreign countries, Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said.
